claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Intrinsic lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr promote distributed dislocation motion and relieve local stress concentrations.
The processed WTaTiVZr alloy contains a fine distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates.
The coherent nanoprecipitates in WTaTiVZr may be Ti-rich phases.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitates relieve stress concentrations that would otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
WTaTiVZr produced by powder metallurgy or similar processing is predominantly BCC.
Pure tungsten has a relatively uniform lattice and a high ductile-brittle transition temperature.
Lattice distortion in the HEA impedes localized dislocation pile-up.
The combined lattice-distortion and nanoprecipitate mechanism produces more uniform plastic deformation.
Pure tungsten has fewer available slip systems and greater stress localization than WTaTiVZr under the proposed conditions.
Pure tungsten has limited dislocation mobility that promotes brittle failure under the comparison conditions.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit lower creep displacement or creep rate than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher strain to failure and ductility than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is applicable when dislocation-mediated plasticity is active, particularly above tungsten's ductile-brittle transition temperature.
Changes in nanoprecipitate size or distribution, nanoprecipitate instability, or grain-boundary segregation may alter the mechanical behavior.
Prior refractory-HEA studies support both lattice distortion and coherent nanoprecipitates as contributors to enhanced ductility.
